sentences.text:
This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C.
against the order of framing of charges against the petitioner under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471 of IPC, 1860 passed by First Additional Sessions Judge, Barwani in S.T No.151/2022 vide dated 19.04.2023.

6) As per prosecution story, complainant lodged a complaint against the applicant stating that he has purchased one second hand tractor No.605 Arjun Model from the applicant in the year 2016 for a consideration of Rs.4,91,000/- for which he has made payment of Rs.2,80,000/- in total, however,
the tractor was not in good working condition therefore he returned the tractor to the applicant for repair.
The applicant neither returned the tractor nor provided another tractor or he refunded the amount paid by the complainant.

On the basis of which a FIR was registered against the applicant bearing crime No.132/2021 for offence punishable under Section 406, 420 of IPC, 1860 and thereafter on completion of investigation the charges under Sections 467, 468 and 471 of IPC has been added against the applicant.

7) During the course of arguments learned counsel for the applicant submits that he is not willing to press the revision with regard to charges framed under Section 420, 406 of IPC, 1860 and he wants to confine his arguments only regarding to offence under Sections 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.

The challenge to the aforesaid order is on the ground that in the entire charge-sheet, there is no material available against the petitioner to indicate that applicant has committed any forgery for earning monetary benefits.
8) In turn Shri Rajesh Joshi, learned Govt. Advocate submitted that there is sufficient material available against the accused with regard to offence under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC.

Complainant has handed over the tractor to the applicant but the applicant has neither returned the consideration of the amount paid by the complainant nor returned back the tractor after repairing the same or provided a new tractor in place of the old one and thereby he has committed breach of trust, which is punishable under Section 406 of IPC.

However, learned Govt. Advocate fairly admitted that as per the case diary nothing can be adverted regarding forgery against the applicant hence offence pertaining to forgery is not made out against the applicant.
9) On due consideration of the rival submissions and on the perusal of the record it is evident that there is nothing on record to prove the offence of forgery against the applicant.

According to Section 228 of Cr.P.C Sessions Judge can frame charges only when if he, after considering and hearing the charges, is of opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence which is exclusively triable by the Court of Session.

However, having gone through the record it is found that that no evidence is available against the applicant by which the Court can presume that the applicant has forged the documents for making any valuable security or transfer of any valuable security.
The prosecution is unable to produce any evidence regarding any forged documents in the Court and nothing has been mentioned regarding that documents in the entire case of the prosecution.

Even while framing of charges the trial Court has not adverted about any forged documents, however, in the order of framing of charge, it is certainly, mentioned that the accused has intentionally forged the documents for the purpose of cheating and dishonest use.

Nevertheless,
it is not mentioned as to which documents has been forged by the applicant.

Hence this Court is of Kanwaljeet Singh Gandhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76794990/

10) In view of the aforesaid discussion in the entirety of the impugned order regarding framing of charges under Section 467, 468 and 471 of IPC, 1860 suffers from illegality and irregularity,
therefore, the charges framed under Section 467, 468 and 471 of IPC are not sustainable, therefore,
in the wake of the aforesaid findings the matter has been remanded back to the Court of First Additional Sessions Judge, Barwani to proceed accordingly.
